Consider a hurdle model: classifier for gap==0 times regressor on nonzero, optionally log target. Community norms: (1) Every experiment = a dir with run.py that trains on $DATA_DIR/<ds>/train.csv; without $EVAL_DIR it writes 5-fold CV error (KFold(5,shuffle=True,random_state=0), same metric as meta.json) to $OUT_DIR/metrics.json, also include baseline CV error from /lab/data/baselines/materials_baseline.py computed in the same run; with $EVAL_DIR set it trains on all train.csv and writes $OUT_DIR/predictions.csv (id,pred) for $EVAL_DIR/<ds>/inputs.csv. Run via 'lab exec DIR -- python run.py'. Only claim numbers from metrics.json. Publish only if CV beats baseline clearly (>=5% relative). (2) Also save out-of-fold predictions and useful features to $OUT_DIR (e.g. oof.csv) so others can build on them, and post blob ids on the board. (3) Collaboration counts only when you consume another member's accepted artifact outputs via --input and add a relation extends/corrects/refutes; actively look at 'lab artifacts' and build on teammates' work (stacking, adding features, correcting). Keep runs < 10 min, use n_jobs<=4 (16 CPUs shared). Session is 60 min: publish a first solid result within ~25 min, then iterate.

artifacts.summary: Re-ran agent-845155b8's findin-86363fec code verbatim. Features use compositions only and no labels, so I found no leakage. Seed1: 0.1147 vs 0.1196 (4.2%). Seed2: 0.1182 vs 0.1260 (6.2%). Mean: 0.1164 vs 0.1228 (5.2%). Group CV: 0.1882 vs 0.2000 (5.9%). The blend wins on every split scheme, but the relative gain on new seeds (5.2%) is below the claimed 6.7%. Group CV error is ~60% higher than random CV for both models, so random-KFold glass errors are optimistic for unseen chemical systems.
